questions.q: In the Meridian Outfitters timeline objection, what does the model answer do instead of claiming the nine-month plan is risk-free?
options: It argues the panel is wrong to raise the concern at all
It abandons the plan entirely and proposes starting over with a new timeline
It names the specific delivery risk (cross-team coordination) and states a sequencing mitigation that ships the lowest-coordination workstream first
It claims the three regional teams will magically start coordinating well without any specific plan
questions.explain: The model answer treats the panel's skepticism as valid and responds with concrete sequencing logic rather than false confidence that the timeline was always comfortable.

questions.q: What governance mechanism does this lesson recommend for keeping a platform like Carrow Equipment's governable after launch, when multiple teams make ongoing changes?
options: Letting each team make changes directly in production with no shared process
Freezing all configuration changes permanently after go-live
Requiring every change to be approved by the original system architect personally, forever
A source-driven development model where metadata changes flow through a single tracked, version-controlled repository rather than ad hoc direct changes
questions.explain: A source-driven model gives each environment a traceable, version-controlled source of truth, which is the specific release discipline this lesson names for avoiding uncoordinated changes colliding in production.

questions.q: Why does the model answer to the Fenwick State University "what if the builder leaves" objection point to EDA's standard affiliation and relationship objects?
options: Because a design built on the platform's own standard, documented patterns is maintainable by any admin or architect familiar with that pattern, not just the original builder
Because EDA objects cannot be extended by anyone other than their original creator
Because standard objects are always technically superior to custom ones in every scenario
Because this objection is actually about data residency, not maintainability
questions.explain: The strength of this answer is that it avoids tribal-knowledge risk by relying on a widely-understood standard pattern rather than an undocumented custom structure only the original builder understood.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why do delivery and governance objections usually reward the "boring, standard" answer over a clever, scenario-specific one?
options: Because panels always prefer the shortest possible answer regardless of content
Because "clever and fragile" is a worse governance outcome than "standard and maintainable," and these objections test whether the candidate understands that trade-off
Because clever answers are against Salesforce's official certification rules
Because standard answers are always technically simpler to implement than custom ones
questions.explain: Unlike some technical objections where a clever answer genuinely wins, governance objections specifically reward maintainability and predictability over cleverness.

questions.q: What is the main difference between change-set-based release management and a source-driven development model, as described in this lesson?
options: Change sets and source-driven development are functionally identical with different names
Change sets can only be used for Experience Cloud, never for internal orgs
Source-driven development eliminates the need for any environments other than production

A source-driven model routes all changes through a single tracked, version-controlled repository, while an older change-set-based approach moves changes between orgs without that shared, version-controlled source of truth, making simultaneous conflicts harder to catch
questions.explain: The key distinction this lesson draws is the presence (or absence) of a shared, version-controlled source of truth that makes conflicting simultaneous changes easier to catch before they collide in production.
